sentences.text: Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose off the appeal filed u/S 70 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006("FSS Act" in short).

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006("FSS Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Vide the present appeal, the order dated 19.11.2019 has been challenged vide which Ld.Adjudicating Officer/ADM(East) ("AO" in short) imposed a penalty of Rs.30,000/ each on all the appellants.
2. The present appeal has been filed on 06.11.2020 alongwith an application for condonation of delay.
In the application for condonation of delay, it has been submitted that the appeal could not be filed within limitation period due to misconception that the order has to be passed by the court.

It has been submitted that the appellants on 20.02.2020 and 21.02.2020 received notice regarding deposition of Demand Draft of penalty, issued by the respondent and after receiving the above notices, the appellants contacted their previous counsel and one month delay was caused by the previous counsel for his personal reason and thereafter, period of lock down started.
Thus, the appeal could not be filed within limitation period.
Ld. Counsel for the appellants submitted that there was no deliberate attempt on the part of the appellants to cause the delay.
3. Per contra, Ld.Chief PP for respondent has submitted that there is no jurisdiction with the present court to condone the delay.
It has been submitted that limitation period is of 30 days and this court can maximum condone the delay for another 30 days.
4. I have heard the submissions and perused the record.
5. Section 3.3.1 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 ("FSS Rules" in short) provides as under: "3.3.1 Appeal to Appellate tribunal 1. Limitation for filing appeal:

Every appeal under section 70 of the Act, arising out of a decision of the Adjudicating Officer appointed under section 68 of the Act, shall be filed within a period of 30 days from the date on which the copy of the order against which the appeal is filed, is received by the appellant.

Provided, however, that the Appellate Tribunal may allow a maximum of another 30 days to entertain an appeal if it is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing the appeal within first 30 days."

A bare perusal of above FSS Rules, makes it clear that after the expiry of 30 days which is a limitation of filing of the appeal u/S 70 FSS Act, the Appellate Tribunal has a discretion to allow a maximum of another 30 days to entertain the appeal.
This extension can only be granted if the Appellate Tribunal is satisfied that there are sufficient cause for not filing the appeal.
6. The impugned order was passed on 19.11.2019.
I have also perused the record of Ld.AO.

The order sheet dated 04.10.2019 of the Ld.Adjudicating Officer indicates that there was representation on behalf of the appellants on which date the case was reserved for order and thus, it cannot be stated that the appellants were not aware of the proceedings.
Another contention by the Ld.Counsel for the appellants is that there was mis conception that appeal can be filed only after the direction of the court, is also not tenable.
It is a settled proposition that ignorance of law is not an excuse.

I consider that the appeal is barred by time and there is no reason for condonation of delay.
Hence, the same is dismissed.
The appeal is also dismissed accordingly.
